binders: Universally quantify pressure and velocity, each an arbitrary function from R to functions R → R, equivalently a real-valued function of two real variables.
Universally quantify bulkModulus, density, x and t as real numbers. The first function argument is the coordinate x and the second is the coordinate t.
Under the hypothesis density ≠ 0, assert an equivalence at the chosen pair (x,t).

On the right side, existentially quantify real numbers pt, px, ut and ux, in that order, inside the scope of pressure, velocity, bulkModulus, density, x and t. The nested witnesses may depend on those outer parameters and syntactically on earlier witnesses; all six conjuncts use the same four chosen numbers.
The variables τ and ξ are bound dummy variables of the one-variable functions being differentiated.
conclusions: LocalDef001 pressure velocity bulkModulus density x t holds if and only if there exist pt, px, ut, ux ∈ R satisfying all the following conditions.
The derivative of τ ↦ pressure(x,τ) at τ = t exists and equals pt.
The derivative of ξ ↦ pressure(ξ,t) at ξ = x exists and equals px.
The derivative of τ ↦ velocity(x,τ) at τ = t exists and equals ut.
The derivative of ξ ↦ velocity(ξ,t) at ξ = x exists and equals ux.
mathematical_definitions: LocalDef001 is an abbreviation for LocalDef002.
LocalDef002 is defined to be exactly the existence of the four derivative values with the four derivative assertions and two equations stated in the conclusion.
All derivatives are ordinary real derivatives of one-variable slices on the full real line, with the other coordinate fixed.

Writing p = pressure, u = velocity, K = bulkModulus and ρ = density, the equations are ∂p/∂t(x,t) + K·∂u/∂x(x,t) = 0 and ∂u/∂t(x,t) + (1/ρ)·∂p/∂x(x,t) = 0, together with existence of all four displayed partial derivatives.
The coefficient parameters K and ρ are real scalars, not functions of the coordinates.
translation.proposition_plain_english: For every pair of real-valued functions pressure and velocity of two real variables, every real bulkModulus, every nonzero real density, and every real pair (x,t), the predicate LocalDef001 holds at these arguments exactly when all four first partial derivatives of pressure and velocity with respect to their two coordinates exist at (x,t), and their values satisfy pressure_t + bulkModulus·velocity_x = 0 and velocity_t + pressure_x/density = 0 there. Since LocalDef001 expands through LocalDef002 to exactly those conditions, this proposition is a definitional equivalence.

restrictions_and_vacuity_risks: The explicit density restriction is nonzero, not positive; negative density is permitted. bulkModulus is unrestricted and may be zero or negative.

The nonzero-density hypothesis is unnecessary for the definitional equivalence itself. Both sides are defined even at density = 0 because real inversion is total with 0⁻¹ = 0, but the stated implication gives no information for density = 0.
The functions are defined on all real coordinate pairs. There is no restriction such as positive time, a spatial interval, or a boundary domain; derivatives are not one-sided or relative to a subset.
The equivalence is evaluated at an arbitrary specified point. It does not assert that either predicate holds there, or that these functions satisfy the equations at every point.
If any required derivative does not exist, both sides of the equivalence are false, and the equivalence still holds.
Only the four slice derivatives at the specified point are required. Joint differentiability, continuity of the partial derivatives, neighborhood regularity and second derivatives are not encoded.
The declaration provides no existence or uniqueness theorem for pressure or velocity, no initial or boundary conditions, and no additional physical constraints associated with their names.
